jobs.title: Senior Director Finance
jobs.description:
Ontario Medical Supply is a Leading Distributor of medical equipment, supplies, and services for healthcare organizations and home healthcare clients across Ontario. Specializing in long term care, assisted living, retirement and home health care. Ontario Medical Supply is partnered for success with Royal Drugs. Royal Drugs is a healthcare company providing specialty pharmacy, infusion therapy, and retail pharmacy services. Together, we work towards supporting optimal health outcomes and better quality of life.

Come Join Our Team!

Purpose:

Reporting to the CFO, the Senior Director, Finance is a managerial role who oversees financial matters for our companies. With a hands-on approach to all aspects of an organization’s finances, the successful candidate will be responsible for the financial activities of the organization to maximize a company’s profits and plan for its growth. The role includes analyzing data and advising the CEO and CFO on ways to use that information to make strategic decisions about the organization’s future.

Position:
Senior Director, Finance
Location:
Ontario Medical Supply. – Mississauga (2785 Skymark Ave, Mississauga, ON L4W 4Y3),
No. of Positions:
1
ATR:
#5251
Type:
Full Time, Permanent
Salary:
$140,000-190,000/year

Job Responsibilities:

Provide leadership to the financial reporting team in a fast-paced, efficient work environment in order to meet deliverables - high-quality, accurate and time-sensitive output.
Collaborate with FP&A team to ensure consistent reporting and processes across the portfolio companies.
Review financial processes and policies across portfolio companies to ensure accurate and consistent consolidation of financial reporting.
Prepare reporting packages to executive leadership and Board of Directors.
Reviewing and advising on legal agreements as required, while considering impacts on other areas (insurance, leasing, credit agreements, supply agreements etc).
Developing reporting packages and forecast models used for raising capital.
Overseeing company compliance with various regulations and legislation.
Managing the end-to-end aspects and preparing memos for strategic projects, including data gathering, cross functional collaboration, communicating issues and management of those issues with key stakeholders.
Knowledge of the following areas is beneficial: mergers and acquisitions, contracts, consolidation, inventory management, treasury.

Qualifications:

University degree supplemented by a Canadian professional accounting designation or a similar designation (e.g. CPA, CA; MBA).
7-10 years of progressive experience in financial and business management.
Strong writing skills to produce business cases, reports, briefings, and requirements documentation.
Experience in review of legal documents and contracts.
Demonstrated experience leveraging strong verbal, and communication skills to prepare and deliver presentations, including senior executives.

Skills:

Ability to work independently to achieve results yet still able to maintain a collaborative approach when required.
Ability to manage deadlines.
Proficient in Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
Excellent research and analytical skills to participate in the review of current practices/processes, and the development of new processes, to assess impacts of changes on the organization and external stakeholders.
Highly developed business acumen.

Human Resources:

While we thank you for your interest, only select applicants will be contacted regarding the position.

Ontario Medical Supply is an inclusive and equal opportunity employer committed to providing diversity and accommodations for applicants upon request at any stage of the recruitment process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) and the Ontario Human Rights Code. All applicants must make their requirements known when contacted.

The company reserves the right to close the competition based on business need and a sufficient pool of candidates who have applied.

AI will be used in the recruitment process.

jobs.title: Director, Inventory Planning & Replenishment
jobs.description:
About The Role

Reporting to the Interim CEO, Performance & N9NE, the Director, Inventory Planning & Replenishment
is responsible for improving product availability and inventory health by ensuring the right approved products are available in the right quantities and locations, at the right time. The Director builds reliable forecasting and replenishment processes and drives effective use of Streamline demand-planning software while balancing customer service and inventory investment.
The Director leads planning and replenishment for Performance and N9NE and develops common planning methods with Source. This is a hands-on leadership role: it combines operating accountability, team development and planning-process improvement with strong cross-functional coordination across Customer Service, Purchasing, Warehousing and Logistics. The Director partners with Source's planning lead on common methods and Streamline adoption; Source retains its planning and replenishment execution and existing reporting structure.
The immediate priorities are reliable replenishment, effective use of Streamline and stronger internal capability.

Main Responsibilities

Forecasting

•Build rolling demand and supply plans from sales history, commercial input, product plans and supplier constraints. Test commercial assumptions and translate agreed demand into inventory requirements.
•Measure forecast error and bias at relevant replenishment horizons. Separate underlying demand, projects and growth assumptions; reconcile intercompany demand to avoid double-counting.
•Lead the demand-planning review with Sales and Product as part of the monthly planning cycle, reviewing and adjusting forecasts for trends, projects, promotions and new items.
Replenishment and inventory health
•Own Performance/N9NE replenishment plans and decisions within delegated limits: which approved items to buy or transfer, how much, when and where. Work with Purchasing and Operations to ensure approved replenishment plans are executed and exceptions are resolved.
•Maintain planning parameters, including lead times, safety stock, service targets, minimum/maximum levels, order cycles and supplier minimum order quantities (MOQs).
•Manage shortage, excess, slow-moving and obsolete inventory exposure. Recommend recovery, transfer and run-out actions; escalate material cash commitments, write-offs and service trade-offs.
•Use ABC/XYZ segmentation to set differentiated service levels, planning parameters and inventory policies.

Demand planning / Streamline ownership

•Establish the planning rules and logic for Streamline, including forecasting and replenishment parameters, workflow design, testing, user training and adoption. Maintain internal ownership after go-live.
•Partner with Source on its planning workflows and adoption. Work with IT, the implementation provider and named data owners on technical delivery, data validation and issue resolution.
•Manage planning milestones and issues, validate licence needs against actual workflows and test replenishment outputs. Embed routine planning in Streamline, with documented exceptions and overrides.

Review discipline and common methods

•Run weekly replenishment reviews and a practical monthly demand, supply and inventory review for Performance/N9NE. Present service, inventory and cash trade-offs for business-leader decisions.
•Lead agreed KPI definitions, planning controls and Streamline methods with Source. Sequence improvements against the agreed work plan and available capacity.

Inventory network planning

•Set and manage inventory-transfer rules within approved service and inventory targets; agree transfer frequency with Operations, balancing availability, inventory investment and freight cost.
•Evaluate hub-and-spoke replenishment with Operations and implement the agreed inventory-planning approach.
•Define stocked versus non-stocked item strategy by location.

Product lifecycle inventory planning

•Translate supplier lead times, minimum orders, production availability, container constraints and warehouse capacity into inventory plans. Purchasing and Operations retain supplier-order follow-up and physical execution.
•Develop first-buy, launch-stock, phased-receipt and run-out plans with Product and commercial teams. Quantify inventory exposure before commitments; Product/Sourcing retains product and supplier decisions.

People, knowledge and reporting

•Develop assigned planners, assess capacity and establish documented workflows and backup coverage. Capture critical operating knowledge and strengthen the team’s independence.
•Publish an inventory and availability scorecard with root causes, actions and owners. Work with Finance to validate benefits and with data owners to resolve planning-data issues.

Knowledge and Experience

•Typically, 8–12+ years of relevant demand, inventory or replenishment planning experience, including people leadership and cross-functional change.
•Proven improvement in availability and inventory health in multi-location distribution, imported finished goods, furniture, building products or a comparable inventory-intensive business.
•Hands-on delivery of planning-platform implementation or adoption. Streamline experience is an asset; broader planning and implementation capability is essential.
•Strong command of forecasting, safety stock, supplier lead times, service targets, order constraints, multi-location replenishment, working-capital trade-offs, ERP data and analytical tools.
•Experience establishing practical demand/supply reviews, developing planners and working constructively with Sales, Product, Purchasing, Operations and Finance.
•Relevant degree or equivalent experience; relevant planning or supply-chain certification is an asset. Ability to work from Burnaby and travel to Canadian and U.S. operating locations as required.
•A practical, hands-on builder who combines analytical depth with commercial judgement. The Director respects existing expertise, challenges assumptions constructively, explains decisions clearly and develops capability that stays with the organisation.

jobs.title: Director, Real Estate Finance
jobs.description:
A career as a Director in the Real Estate Finance team of the Commercial & Private Banking 1859 sector at the National Bank means supporting the best players in the real estate sector both in their interim construction projects and in their long-term financing needs. This job allows you to have a positive impact on our clients and our organization by combining your experience with large-value real estate banking transactions and your passion for business development.   Your job:
  Identify and develop business opportunities in your market, increase your commercial client base, and establish business development strategies
  Help your clients attain their business objectives by proposing financial strategies based on the most suitable combination of Bank products and services
  Meet clients' changing needs by adapting and optimizing financial products and sales approaches
  Negotiate the terms and conditions of agreements with clients, while making sure that they meet risk management standards and profitability criteria
  Create and execute sales and business development plans in collaboration with the Real Estate Financing Group’s annual goals;
  Manage, develop and maintain an existing portfolio including, but not limited to, credit underwriting and analysis of annual reviews, writing of new business, and exhibiting strong risk management skills;
  Work in collaboration with the all the team across Canada, to reach our objectives of increased revenues and continuous improvement.
  Identify the risks inherent to the sector activities.

Your team:
Within the Commercial & Private Banking 1859 sector you are part of a large team and you report to the Director and Team Lead of Real Estate Financing for the Calgary market. Our team stands out for our expertise, our speed to market and our entrepreneurial spirit. This position offers a hybrid work mode; you organize your weeks between the office, home and meetings with customers.  Prerequisites :
  Bachelor's degree and/or Master’s degree in a related field
  Minimum of 5 years of real estate financing experience
  Business development and negotiation experience
  Knowledge of banking products and services for real estate businesses
  Strong interpersonal and writing skills
  Experience in commercial credit underwriting and evidence of strong business and financial analytical skills
  Be a team player

Languages: English
Required skills: Accountability, Client-focused, Communication, Emotional Intelligence, Learning Agility, Listening, Teamwork

Your benefits

In addition to competitive compensation, upon hiring you’ll be eligible for a wide range of flexible benefits to help promote your wellbeing and that of your family such as:

* Health and wellness program, including many options
* Flexible group insurance
* Generous pension plan
* Employee Share Ownership Plan
* Employee and family assistance program
* Preferential banking services
* Involvement in community initiatives
* Telemedicine service
* Virtual sleep clinic

We have an offer that keeps up with trends as well as your needs and those of your family.

Our dynamic work environments and cutting-edge collaboration tools foster a positive employee experience. We value employees’ ideas. Whether through our surveys or programs, regular feedback and ongoing communication are encouraged.

Making a bold move in a people-first environment

We’re a bank on a human scale that stands out for its courage, entrepreneurial culture, and passion for people. Our mission is to have a positive impact on people’s lives. Our core values of partnership, agility, and empowerment inspire us, and inclusion is central to our commitments. We aim, wherever possible, to provide a barrier-free and accessible environment to all employees.

We strive to provide accessibility measures throughout the recruitment process within the limits of our available resources. If you require accommodations, feel free to let us know during our initial conversations. We welcome all candidates! What can you bring to our team?

Join us!
